source.title: Data efficiency and extrapolation trends in neural network interatomic potentials

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses random-label memorization as background, but its own generalization results concern noisy regression labels and out-of-distribution molecular configurations. It does not test the same-distribution generalization claim or any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on fitting random labels but does not reproduce that experiment. Its own noisy-label and extrapolation results are recorded under fits_no_version; out-of-distribution results do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures noisy molecular regression, extrapolation error, MD stability, and learning-curve slopes. It does not test any listed version: additive force noise does not establish fixed random-label memorization, and loss entropy versus extrapolation or stability does not measure sharpness versus training–test gaps. Its optimizer experiments compare Adam variants, without an SGD comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that NNIPs can recover underlying potential energy surfaces despite added noise, possibly through data redundancy, and that loss entropy can help predict extrapolation error, MD stability, and data efficiency. They also emphasize that in-domain RMSE fails to predict stability in the high-accuracy regime and that loss-entropy comparisons have architectural limitations.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains interatomic-potential regressors on molecular energy and force data and evaluates noisy-label recovery, extrapolation, and simulation stability; it does not use the claim's image or language classification setting.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that architecture and training choices, including rescaling, optimizer settings, message-passing depth, and MACE symmetry order, change extrapolation or MD stability. These are out-of-distribution outcomes, not the claim's same-distribution gap.

fits_no_version.finding: Four NNIPs resist fitting additive Gaussian force noise on 3BPA while predicting uncorrupted forces below the noise baseline. Additional ANI-Al experiments show analogous denoising, including much larger energy noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These molecular potential regressors can recover underlying energy or force relationships despite additive training-target noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Filter-normalized loss entropy generally correlates with extrapolation performance, MD stability, and learning-curve slopes. It fails to recover stability trends across MACE symmetry orders and underperforms force RMSE for the two-layer NequIP optimizer comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss entropy can predict molecular potential robustness and data efficiency in some architecture and training comparisons, with limitations in comparability across architectural changes.

fits_no_version.finding: AMSGrad improves extrapolation and simulation stability relative to baseline Adam; MACE's combined stochastic weight averaging and weight cycling also improves stability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam configuration and weight-averaging strategies affect molecular potential extrapolation and simulation stability.

record.code_released: https://github.com/marcellodebernardi/loss-landscapes; paper states additional reproduction code/data would be made available after internal review at LLNL.
record.problems: The noisy-label result is reported qualitatively in the prose, with detailed values only in a figure. The experiments use molecular regression and do not test arbitrary labels or same-distribution classification generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for each noise level or model were extracted because the text does not state their individual outcomes numerically or describe them separately; Fig. 1a contains the plotted results.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside above-chance natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD under limited and broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that mitigate large-batch penalties.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes, strengths, and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking training–test gaps among similarly fitted convolutional models, including comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion rests on the measured constructs, not merely on the molecular domain or use of out-of-distribution evaluation. No additional results bearing on V1–V8 require missing-row entries.

versions.untested_parts: Arbitrary-label fitting and same-distribution generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the zero-training-error interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers' same-distribution held-out performance on image or language benchmarks.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout's effect on same-distribution test error.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness ranks same-distribution training-test gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring same-distribution test accuracy.

rows.subject: four different NNIPs (models listed in Fig. 1a)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on 3BPA forces with gradually corrupted labels; training error evaluated on the noisy data.

conditions.value: σ ranging from 0.0 to 0.1; noise added to forces

rows.measure: Training force RMSE on noisy data
rows.value: With noise, training loss plateaued instead of tending to zero; noisy-force prediction saturated at the noise limit.
rows.note: The text reports the result across the four models without giving separate numeric values in the prose.
rows.check: The reported plateau is supported, but it measures resistance to additive Gaussian force noise, not V1's random-label fitting. Specify the four models: MACE (v=2, L=0), MACE (v=2, L=3), NequIP (n=2, L=3), and NequIP (n=5, L=3). These experiments train only on forces. The noise standard deviation is σ times σDFT, with σDFT=0.95 eV/Å.

rows.subject: four different NNIPs (models listed in Fig. 1a)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated models trained on corrupted 3BPA force labels against the original, uncorrupted data.

conditions.value: σ ranging from 0.0 to 0.1; noise added to training forces

rows.measure: Force RMSE on original data relative to the noise baseline
rows.value: Substantially smaller than the noise baseline.
rows.note: The result concerns denoising continuous force labels, not arbitrary-label memorization or same-distribution classification generalization.
rows.check: Below-noise-baseline error is supported, but evaluation against the original uncorrupted dataset does not establish an independent held-out comparison or V1's natural-label/random-label contrast. Specify the same four models as R1 and force-only training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
